chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who sees blood on his garment, then forgets to wash it until he performs salat (prayer). He said: “He repeats his salat, so that he may pay attention to a thing when it is on his garment, as a punishment for his forgetfulness.” I said: Then what should one do who did not know? Should he repeat when he notices it? He said: “No, but he starts afresh.”

And these two reports indicate the obligation of removing blood from the garment. As for the amount which, when it reaches it, its removal becomes obligatory, the first report contains its clarification, and it also indicates it.

key_terms.الْخَبَرَانِ: the two reports cited as evidence
key_terms.ثَوْبِهِ: his garment or clothing worn in salat
key_terms.يَسْتَأْنِفُ: he begins anew or resumes from the start
key_terms.يَغْسِلَهُ: to wash and remove the impurity
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he repeats the salat after the defect is known

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone prays wearing a garment with blood on it?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on praying in a garment stained with blood. It distinguishes between one who knew of the blood and forgot to wash it, and one who was unaware, showing the legal importance of removing najasah from clothing for salat.
